newsitem.title: USA: Boeing suppliers seen boosted by its succes.
newsitem.headline: Boeing suppliers seen boosted by its succes.

text.p: Companies which provide parts and services to Boeing Co could be set for good times, with the Seattle-based aerospace company having taken over both McDonnell Douglas Corp and Rockwell International, according to a U.S. weekly business newspaper.
The company and its vendors are enjoying an order and delivery surge which began in 1995 and is still building momentum, Barron's said in its February 17 issue.
"Vendors see nothing but blue skies immediately ahead for their sales and profits," the paper said. "And that should be good news for their stock prices, some of which have already moved up sharply."

Parker Hannifin Corp said in Barron's it bills $700,000 worth of components for each Boeing 777 produced. Northrop Grumman Corp gets several million dollars for making the main fuselage of each Boeing 747, the paper said.
Other key Boeing aircraft components were made by AlliedSignal Inc, B.F. Goodrich Co, Honeywell Inc, Sundstrand Corp, Trinova Corp and Ametek Inc, the newspaper said.

Some smaller companies were feeling the impact of Boeing's boom even more, Barron's said. These included Curtiss-Wright Corp, Moog Inc, BE Aerospace Inc, Coltec Industries Inc, SPS Technologies Inc and Fairchild Corp, it said.
